screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/video_settings/video_settings_screen
screen.about: The window, the frame rate and the graphics.

row.label: WINDOW
row.help: How the game takes the screen. Fullscreen sets the display to the game's resolution. Borderless covers it with a window that others open over. Windowed is a window to move and resize. F11 switches between the two.

row.label: RESOLUTION
row.help: What fullscreen and borderless draw at. Native is the display's own, the sharpest; a lower one is lighter on a slow computer, and softer. Fullscreen sets the display to it; borderless scales it.

row.label: WINDOW SIZE
row.help: The window's size: 4:3 first, then 16:10, 16:9 and 21:9. Its edges can also be dragged.

row.label: REFRESH RATE
row.help: How many times a second the display shows a picture while the game is fullscreen. Auto keeps the display's own. VSync and Max FPS's Auto follow it.

row.label: FRAME RATE & SYNC ›
row.help: VSync, variable refresh (G-SYNC, FreeSync), the most frames a second and low latency.

row.label: FIELD OF VIEW
row.help: How wide you see on foot, in degrees across 16:9. Default is the Xbox's. Above 150 needs Panini Projection. Passengers use it too; driver and gunner: First Person.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type 20 to 160. Capped at 110 in Pro 2v2 games.

row.label: ORIENTATION
row.help: Which way up you hold the device. Portrait has a strip of buttons along the top, the picture under it and the touch controls below it. Auto turns with the device.

row.label: SCREEN LAYOUT ›
row.help: Where the picture sits on a screen taller than it, its shape, and the frame around it in portrait.

row.label: FIRST PERSON ›
row.help: The vehicles' and scopes' fields of view, the Panini projection, how far you see, the reticle, a passenger's view, and your weapon, body and shields.

row.label: STARTUP MOVIES
row.help: Plays the Xbox's intro movie as the game starts, and its attract movies on an idle main menu. Any button skips the intro.
row.note: They are the bink folder of your Xbox disc image, copied with the maps. Without them, put the disc's bink folder beside your maps folder.

row.label: QUALITY
row.help: Enhanced: smoother edges, sharper textures and shadows, smoother lighting. Classic looks as the Xbox did.
row.note: Changing one shows CUSTOM.

row.label: HIGH-RES TEXT
row.help: Draws text and titles with sharp high-resolution fonts. Off draws the game's own.

row.label: BATTERY SAVER
row.help: Up to 60 frames a second and Classic graphics, for a longer battery and a cooler device. Auto turns it on while the device runs on its battery. Your own settings come back as it turns off.

row.label: BRIGHTNESS ›
row.help: How bright the picture is: its gamma, and on an HDR display, HDR's look, how bright white and the HUD are, and the display's peak.

row.label: ADVANCED GRAPHICS ›
row.help: Render resolution, anti-aliasing, texture filtering, model detail, shadows, the lighting and the shields' glow, smooth motion and the tick rate.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/audio_settings/audio_settings_screen
screen.about: The sound and its devices, 3D audio, the volumes and voice chat.

row.label: OUTPUT DEVICE
row.help: Where the game's sound and the other players' voices play.

row.label: 3D AUDIO
row.help: Where the sounds around you come from. Auto and Headphones place each ahead, behind, above or below you, as the Xbox's 3D audio did on speakers and headphones alike; Speakers pans them left and right.

row.label: REVERB
row.help: Echoes sounds as the place you are in would, and muffles those behind walls, as the Xbox did. It costs a little of the processor.

row.label: RESAMPLER
row.help: How sounds are converted to your speakers' rate. Xbox sounds as the Xbox did; Clean is clearer; Classic is brighter but harsher. Xbox and Classic cost a little less.

row.label: SOUND
row.help: Turns all sound off or on, at once.

row.label: MASTER VOLUME
row.help: The volume of everything the game plays. 10 is the Xbox's level; up to 20 is louder.

row.label: MUSIC VOLUME
row.help: The music's volume.

row.label: EFFECTS VOLUME
row.help: Every other sound: weapons, vehicles, the world and the characters' speech.

row.label: VOICE CHAT
row.help: Talk to the other players in network games: while Push to Talk is held (Key Bindings sets its key), whenever you speak, or never.

row.label: INPUT DEVICE
row.help: The microphone voice chat listens to.

row.label: VOICE VOLUME
row.help: How loud the other players' voices are.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.
Leaves Settings without keeping any change.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/mouse_settings/mouse_settings_screen
screen.about: The mouse, the controller and the keys.

row.label: SENSITIVITY
row.help: How far the view turns as the mouse moves, on Counter-Strike 2's scale: your CS2 number turns the same here. Drag the slider, or press left and right. Click the number (or press A) to type an exact value, e.g. 1.7, then press Enter.
row.note: No acceleration.

row.label: VERTICAL SENSITIVITY
row.help: How far the view turns up and down, of how far it turns side to side. 1X turns it as far.

row.label: ZOOM AIM SPEED
row.help: How fast you turn while zoomed in. CS2 matches Counter-Strike 2's scoped feel; Original is how Halo felt.
row.note: Mouse only: controllers always turn as Halo did.

row.label: INVERT MOUSE
row.help: Moving the mouse forward looks down, as a flight stick does.

row.label: MOUSE AIM ASSIST
row.help: Slows and drags your aim along with a target while you aim with the mouse, as it does with a controller.
row.note: Off in Pro 2v2 games, for everyone.

row.label: INSTANT AIM
row.help: Turns the view the moment the mouse moves, not up to two of the game's updates later. Off feels as the original did.
row.note: Off for everyone in a Pro 2v2 Classic game; yours again after it.

row.label: MENU CURSOR
row.help: The menus' blue arrow for the mouse, and its size. The sizes keep their share of the screen at any resolution.
row.note: Off shows the system's pointer.

row.label: KEY BINDINGS ›
row.help: The keys and mouse buttons for each action, two for each.

row.label: BUTTON PROMPTS
row.help: The buttons the HUD's prompts show. Auto shows the keys or the controller's buttons, as you last played with.

row.label: CONTROLLER ›
row.help: The look sensitivity and inversion, the button and stick layouts, and vibration, kept in your player profile.

row.label: VR SETUP ›
row.help: Your hands, aiming, turning, your height, the HUD and the menus in VR.

row.label: CROUCH
row.help: Hold crouches while the button is held, as Halo did. Toggle crouches at a tap until you press it again, jump, take a seat or die; holding it still crouches while held.

row.label: CROUCH WALK
row.help: Off: a full push of the stick stands you up from a crouch, as Halo did. On: you stay crouched and walk at a crouch's speed.
row.note: The touch controls always stay crouched.

row.label: TOUCH CROUCH
row.help: The touch controls' Crouch. Toggle crouches at a tap until the next tap, a jump, a seat or death; Hold crouches while your finger is on it.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.
Leaves Settings without keeping any change.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/network_setup/network_settings_screen
screen.about: Internet play, sharing maps and updates.

row.label: INTERNET PLAY
row.help: Host and join games over the internet with invite links, and find public games. Off keeps to the local network.

row.label: OPEN ROUTER PORT
row.help: Asks your router to open the game's port (UPnP), so that players can reach the games you host.

row.label: JOIN FROM CLIPBOARD
row.help: Joins a game when you switch to the game with its invite link copied.

row.label: DISCORD ACCOUNT ›
row.help: Link your Discord account, so that servers that block VPNs let you in while you use one.

row.label: SERVER BROWSER FILTERS ›
row.help: Which games the server browser and the local network's list show: full and empty games, a password, the ping, the game types, and words to search for.

row.label: STREAMER MODE ›
row.help: Hides offensive words in names and text from other players, maps and mods, as stars.

row.label: WEAPON PICKUP
row.help: Multiplayer, with a weapon slot empty: Hold picks up a weapon as you hold the action button, as on the Xbox; Walk Over as you walk over it, as in Custom Edition. Online: the host's choice.

row.label: DOWNLOAD MAPS
row.help: Joining a game on a Custom Edition map you do not have downloads it from the players, if they share it.

row.label: HELP SEND MAPS
row.help: In another player's game, sends its map to the players who join without it, as a torrent's peers do.

row.label: UPLOAD LIMIT
row.help: The most of your upload that sending maps takes, so that the game keeps the rest.

row.label: CHECK FOR UPDATES
row.help: Looks for a new version when the game starts.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/interface_settings/interface_settings_screen
screen.about: The HUD, the players' names, the scoreboard and the chat.

row.label: HIGH-RES HUD
row.help: Draws the HUD from sharp high-resolution redraws. Off draws the game's own pictures.

row.label: BUTTON STYLE
row.help: The buttons the HUD draws. Classic: plain Xbox buttons. Gems: shaded Xbox buttons. Dark Gems: the menus' button artwork.

row.label: SPARTAN LINK
row.help: Your living teammates' views in the HUD's top line, with their names, shields and distances, in co-op and team games: the SPARTAN LINK key (or D-pad Down) shows and hides them. Off: the key does nothing.

row.label: PLAYER NAMES
row.help: In multiplayer, whose names are drawn above their heads.

row.label: NAME SIZE
row.help: How large the players' names are drawn.

row.label: SCOREBOARD
row.help: A team game's scoreboard: a column for each team, or every player in order of score.

row.label: SCOREBOARD PANEL
row.help: Draws a dark panel behind the scoreboard, for clearer text.

row.label: WHILE DEAD
row.help: While you wait to respawn in co-op or a team game: watch a living teammate through their eyes (A or Jump for the next), or the game's death camera.

row.label: MATCH TIMER
row.help: Draws a clock at the bottom right in multiplayer, counting up from the start of the game.

row.label: TEXT CHAT
row.help: Shows the text chat. Hide draws none of its lines, and its keys and D-pad Up open nothing.

row.label: CHAT TEXT
row.help: Colors draws the names in their team's color; White draws it all white, as Custom Edition does.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/profile_settings/profile_settings_screen
screen.about: Your player profiles, your name and color, and the disk space the maps and caches take.

row.label: NAME ›
row.help: The name the other players see, kept in your player profile.

row.label: COLOR ›
row.help: Your armor's color in free-for-all multiplayer games, kept in your player profile.

row.label: CREATE PROFILE ›
row.help: Your name, color and controller layout are kept in a player profile. Make one to set them; the rest of Settings works without one.

row.label: MANAGE PROFILES ›
row.help: Switch to another player profile, make a new one or delete one. Your changes so far are kept.

row.label: MAP STORAGE
row.help: Instant Loading keeps every map unpacked, about 3.0 GB, so loads never wait. Disk Space Saver keeps at most 730 MB, saving 2.3 GB or more, little on most drives. A map it has not kept loads a second or more slower.
row.note: Switching back unpacks them in the background.

row.label: CLEAR CACHES
row.help: Deletes what the game keeps only to start and load faster: the unpacked maps, their prepared draws, the menus' pictures, the ambient occlusion's volumes and the GPU's pipelines, made again as you play.
row.note: Select it twice: the first asks, the second clears.

row.label: REPORT A PROBLEM
row.help: Saves a report (the log, your settings and GPU, the frame rate and a screenshot) and opens a GitHub issue filled in with it: say what happened, drag in the report's file, submit. F8 does the same in a game, its screenshot that moment.

row.label: GOAT H1
row.help: Halo: Combat Evolved, the Xbox game, on this computer, played from your own copy of its maps. GOAT H1 is a free fan project.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.
Leaves Settings without keeping any change.

screen.name: main_menu/settings_select/player_setup/player_profile_edit/mods_settings/mods_settings_screen
screen.about: Texture, sound, text and model packs from the mods folder.

row.label: MANAGE MODS ›
row.help: Texture, sound, text and model packs from the mods folder: turn each on or off, and choose which plays over which. They are this computer's, for every profile.

row.label: MODS FOLDER
row.help: Each mod is a folder in the mods folder, beside the maps folder, with its mod.toml and its tags. Mods are turned on and off from the main menu's Settings, not in a game.

button.help: Puts this tab's settings back to their defaults. Nothing changes until OK.
Keeps your changes, on every tab, and applies them.
Leaves Settings without keeping any change.

row.label: RENDER RESOLUTION
row.help: Full draws the game at your screen's resolution. Above 100% draws it larger and scales it down: finer and smoother, for over twice the graphics card's work at 150%, four times at 200%. Xbox draws 640x480, scaled up: softer, and very light.

row.label: ANTI-ALIASING
row.help: Smooths jagged edges. FXAA and SMAA cost little; MSAA is sharper and costs more of the graphics card.

row.label: ANTI-ALIASING
row.help: Smooths jagged edges. FXAA and SMAA cost little; MSAA is sharper and costs more of the graphics card.

row.label: TEXTURE FILTERING
row.help: Keeps floors and walls sharp into the distance, at a small cost. Off looks as the Xbox did: surfaces blur a few steps away.

row.label: MODEL DETAIL
row.help: How detailed characters and vehicles stay in the distance. Xbox simplifies them as on a TV; Full keeps their detail for your screen; Highest always draws the most. Auto is Full in VR.

row.label: SMOOTH MOTION
row.help: Draws movement smoothly between the game's 30 updates a second, so that it looks fluid at any frame rate. Off shows each update as it is.

row.label: SHADOW QUALITY
row.help: How sharp the shadows of characters, vehicles and weapons are. Xbox is the original's soft, blocky shadow; each step up is crisper, and costs a little more of the graphics card.

row.label: SMOOTH LIGHTING
row.help: Lights characters and weapons smoothly, without the flat facets of the Xbox's lighting, at a small cost.

row.label: DYNAMIC LIGHTS
row.help: Enhanced: plasma bolts, muzzle flashes and blasts light their surroundings smoothly, with a glow. Classic lights them as the Xbox did.
row.note: Classic for everyone in a Pro 2v2 game; yours again after it.

row.label: AMBIENT OCCLUSION
row.help: World: soft shade where characters, vehicles and scenery meet the level and each other, from the level's shape; the levels keep their own lighting. Ray Traced: the shade of characters and vehicles traced by the graphics card, where it can (else World).

row.label: SHIELD GLOW
row.help: Shields light their surroundings as they flare, in the shield's own color. Online: the host's choice.
row.note: Off in Pro 2v2 games, for everyone.

row.label: GLOW INTENSITY
row.help: Light Show: the shields' glow reaches three times as far, and is brighter. Online: the host's choice.
row.note: Default in Pro 2v2 games, for everyone.

row.label: TICK RATE
row.help: How often the world updates each second, in games on this device (campaign, split screen, bots). 60 and 120 respond faster and take more of the processor. Online games play at their host's tick rate: a GOAT H1 game's (GOAT H1 60 Tick), a Legacy game's 30.

row.label: ANIMATIONS
row.help: Enhanced: you turn with your aim in a jump and a grenade throw, and your legs keep moving as you throw. Classic moves as the Xbox did, so the AI plays as it did. Online: the host's choice.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: GAMMA
row.help: How bright the picture is, the HUD and menus too, as Halo PC's gamma. Higher brightens the dark parts; lower darkens them. 1.0 shows the game as it is drawn. With HDR on an HDR display, Paper White sets the brightness instead.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from 0.5 to 2.0.

row.label: HDR
row.help: Brighter highlights on an HDR display. Auto turns it on while the display shows HDR; a display without HDR shows the game as it was.

row.label: HDR MODE
row.help: Faithful keeps the picture and brightens its highlights. Punchy lifts the whole scene, as a remaster would.
row.note: The pictures are approximate: SDR cannot show HDR.

row.label: PAPER WHITE
row.help: With HDR, how bright white surfaces and the HUD are, in nits. System matches your system's SDR brightness. Raise it in a bright room.

row.label: UI BRIGHTNESS
row.help: With HDR, how bright the HUD and the menus are, in nits, apart from the picture. Paper White keeps them where paper white is. The HUD's glows stay as far above it.

row.label: DISPLAY PEAK
row.help: The brightest the display shows, and its SDR white, as the system reports them.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: VSYNC
row.help: Shows each frame at a refresh of the display: even motion that never tears. With Low Latency it adds almost no input lag. It is on in the Steam Deck's Game Mode.

row.label: VARIABLE REFRESH
row.help: For a G-SYNC or FreeSync display: VSync on and the frame rate held just under the refresh rate, so each frame shows as soon as it is ready, without tearing. Auto turns it on where the system says VRR is on.

row.label: VRR FRAME CAP
row.help: Frames a second kept under the refresh rate, so the game stays in the screen's VRR range and never falls back to VSync. Lower is closer to the most frames; higher is safer on a screen with a narrow range.
row.note: Used while Variable Refresh is on.

row.label: MAX FPS
row.help: The most frames drawn a second with VSync off. Auto is twice the display's refresh rate. More feels smoother and uses more power; None draws as fast as it can.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type 10 to 1000.

row.label: LOW LATENCY
row.help: With VSync on, starts each frame just in time for the refresh it is shown at, so a press reaches the screen sooner. Off starts each frame as soon as the one before is waiting. Auto is on.

row.label: SHOW FRAME RATE
row.help: Draws the frame rate at the bottom right of the screen, to see how the game runs: the frames drawn each second, averaged over half a second. Green is 30 or more, red under 30.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: VEHICLE FIELD OF VIEW
row.help: How wide you see from a vehicle's third-person seats (driver, gunner), in degrees across a 16:9 screen. Passenger seats use your Field of View. Default keeps the game's view; Match uses your Field of View. Above 150 needs Panini Projection.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from 20 to 160.

row.label: SCOPED FIELD OF VIEW
row.help: How far a scope zooms at your Field of View. Xbox zooms to the same view whatever yours is, as the Xbox did. Scaled zooms your own view by the same magnification, so a wider view stays wider zoomed.

row.label: PANINI PROJECTION
row.help: Stops a wide field of view from stretching what is at the sides; you still see as far, and the middle is drawn larger. 1 keeps their shapes true. The HUD stays flat. Fields of view up to 160 need it.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type 0 to 1.

row.label: PANINI VERTICAL
row.help: With Panini Projection on: straightens floors and ceilings above and below the middle, and stretches the sides taller. 0 keeps their shapes true.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type 0 to 1.

row.label: DRAW DISTANCE
row.help: How far the world is drawn (the far clip), in world units of about 3 meters. Default is the game's 1024, which the stock maps fit in; farther shows more of a large custom map.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from 1024 to 10000.

row.label: LOWERED RETICLE
row.help: Puts the reticle below the middle of the screen, as Halo 2 and 3 do. Your view tilts up a little, so shots still go where the reticle points. Zooming centers it.

row.label: RETICLE LOWERED BY
row.help: How far below the middle the lowered reticle sits, in percent of the screen's height. 10 is about Halo 2's and 3's.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from 0 to 30.

row.label: PASSENGER VIEW
row.help: Riding in a Warthog or a Scorpion in the campaign and co-op: the view from behind the vehicle, or from your seat. Behind, the weapon cannot zoom.

row.label: WEAPON & BODY ›
row.help: Your weapon and hands: whether they are drawn, their field of view and their place. Your legs, and your shield's flare on your arms, its color and an overshield's.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.

row.label: HORIZONTAL
row.help: Moves your weapon and hands right, or left below 0, in centimeters, for every weapon, as far on the screen at any weapon field of view. 0 keeps them where the game puts them. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: VERTICAL
row.help: Moves your weapon and hands up, or down below 0, in centimeters. Lower it to see more of the screen. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: DEPTH
row.help: Pushes your weapon and hands away from you, or closer below 0, in centimeters. Too close and they cut off. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: PITCH
row.help: Tilts your weapon's muzzle up, or down below 0, in degrees, turning it in place. Your shots still go where the reticle points. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: YAW
row.help: Turns your weapon's muzzle right, or left below 0, in degrees. Your shots still go where the reticle points. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: ROLL
row.help: Tilts the top of your weapon right, or left below 0, in degrees. Your shots still go where the reticle points. In a game, Settings from the pause menu also sets the weapon you hold on its own.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: HORIZONTAL
row.help: Moves the weapon you hold right, or left below 0, in centimeters, added to All Weapons'. Each weapon keeps its own, a modded map's too.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: VERTICAL
row.help: Moves the weapon you hold up, or down below 0, in centimeters, added to All Weapons'.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: DEPTH
row.help: Pushes the weapon you hold away, or closer below 0, in centimeters, added to All Weapons'.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -20 to 20.

row.label: PITCH
row.help: Tilts the muzzle of the weapon you hold up, or down below 0, in degrees, added to All Weapons'.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: YAW
row.help: Turns the muzzle of the weapon you hold right, or left below 0, in degrees, added to All Weapons'.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: ROLL
row.help: Tilts the top of the weapon you hold right, or left below 0, in degrees, added to All Weapons'.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from -15 to 15.

row.label: RESET THIS WEAPON
row.help: Puts the weapon you hold back to All Weapons' place: its own offsets go back to 0 when you press OK.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: WEAPON AND HANDS
row.help: Draws your weapon, your hands and what they hold. Hide clears the view; you still fire, reload and hear them.

row.label: WEAPON FIELD OF VIEW
row.help: How wide your weapon and hands are drawn, in degrees across a 16:9 screen: wider draws them smaller. Default keeps the weapon's own view.
row.note: Click the number (or press A) to type any from 20 to 150.

row.label: WEAPON POSITION ›
row.help: Moves and turns your weapon and hands on the screen, for every weapon and, in a game, for the one you hold.

row.label: LEGS
row.help: Your legs when you look down, moving as you run: your body as the others see it.

row.label: ARM SHIELDS
row.help: When your shield takes a hit, its flare shows on your first-person arms too, as on your body, and fades as it does there. A full, untouched shield shows nothing.
row.note: An overshield stays lit on them with Overshield on, below.

row.label: SHIELD COLOR
row.search_choices: white black red blue gray yellow green pink purple cyan cobalt orange teal sage brown tan maroon salmon
row.help: Your shield's flare in an armor color, whatever your armor. Only you see it. Default keeps its own.

row.label: OVERSHIELD
row.help: An overshield stays lit for as long as it lasts, in its own color, on your body and, with Arm Shields, your arms. Off draws it as the original did. Online: the host's choice.
row.note: Off in Pro 2v2 games, for everyone.

row.label: OVERSHIELD COLOR
row.help: The overshield's color as its layers drain, as your shield meter shows them: green while the green layer lasts, then red. Red keeps it red throughout.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: LOOK SENSITIVITY
row.help: How fast the right stick turns the view.

row.label: INVERT LOOK
row.help: Pushing the right stick up looks down.

row.label: INVERT TURNING
row.help: Pushing the right stick right turns the view left. For every controller on this device.

row.label: GYRO & FLICK STICK ›
row.help: Aim by turning a controller that has a gyroscope; the right stick's aim style (Classic or Modern), and the right stick as a flick stick.

row.label: INVERT FLIGHT
row.help: Flying vehicles pitch as aircraft do: pushing up flies down.

row.label: AUTO-CENTER LOOK
row.help: Levels the view while you walk.

row.label: BUTTON LAYOUT
row.search_choices: swap triggers a l trigger b r stick bumper jumper fishsticks recon
row.help: Which of the controller's buttons does what. Button Remapping sets them one by one; the keyboard's keys are Key Bindings'.

row.label: STICK LAYOUT
row.help: Which stick moves and which looks. Southpaw swaps them.

row.label: BUTTON REMAPPING ›
row.help: Put any action on any button, each player their own layout, the D-pad and Back too: chat, push to talk, the scoreboard, a screenshot.

row.label: STICK DEAD ZONES ›
row.help: How far each stick moves before it does anything: more for a worn stick that drifts, less for finer aim.

row.label: VIBRATION
row.help: Rumbles the controller.

row.label: IN-GAME HELP
row.help: Shows the game's hints about its controls.

row.label: CREATE PROFILE ›
row.help: Your name, color and controller layout are kept in a player profile. Make one to set them; the rest of Settings works without one.

row.label: PLAYER
row.help: Whose buttons to edit. Each player's layout is kept apart, and named for the controller they play with. OK saves every player's.

row.label: SHOW
row.help: Which of the actions to show: movement, combat, general, chat and voice, or the debug camera's.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: SHOW
row.help: Which of the actions to show: movement, weapons, actions or communication.

row.label: WALK
row.help: Hold walks while the Walk key is held; Toggle walks from one press to the next. Walking, the movement keys move you slowly, as a stick pushed a little does.

row.label: WALK SPEED
row.help: How fast you walk. Tracker: as fast as you can and still stay off the enemies' motion trackers. Or a part of your full speed.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: GYRO
row.help: Whether a controller with a gyroscope is connected: a DualSense, a DualShock 4, a Switch Pro Controller or Joy-Cons, a Steam Deck.
row.note: With Steam Input, turn it off for GOAT H1.

row.label: GYRO AIMING
row.search_choices: always hold aim pause thumb stick
row.help: Aim by turning the controller, as a mouse; the stick still works. Hold to Aim: only while the gyro button is held. Hold to Pause: except while it is held, to re-center. Thumb on Stick: while your thumb is on the right stick (Steam Deck, Steam Controller).
row.note: No aim assist on the gyro's aim.

row.label: GYRO BUTTON
row.search_choices: touchpad left paddle right capture share bumper trigger stick
row.help: The button that Hold to Aim and Hold to Pause hold. It still does its own action too: Button Remapping can move that.

row.label: SENSITIVITY
row.help: How far the view turns for each degree you turn the controller: 1 as far, 2 twice as far. Press A, or click the number, to type a value.
row.note: Zoomed in: as Zoom Aim Speed sets.

row.label: VERTICAL SENSITIVITY
row.help: How far the view turns up and down, of how far it turns side to side. 1X turns it as far.

row.label: TURN AXIS
row.help: Player Space turns you as you turn the controller about the up direction, however you hold it: flat, upright or between. Local Space turns you about the controller's own axis, as if held flat.

row.label: SMOOTHING
row.help: Steadies the smallest motions, your hand's tremor, but never a real turn. Off: every motion as it comes.

row.label: CALIBRATE
row.help: Put the controller down on something still, then select this: it measures the gyroscope at rest for a second and a half.
row.note: It also does so whenever it is held still.

row.label: AIM STYLE
row.help: Classic aims as the original: a diagonal turns faster, and can speed up the turn as a full push does. Modern aims as MCC's: the same speed whichever way you push, and only a push straight to the side speeds up the turn.
row.note: The mouse and touch controls are not changed.

row.label: ACCELERATION ANGLE
row.help: Modern aim: how far from straight to the side, in degrees, a full push still speeds up the turn. Lower keeps more diagonals from speeding it up.

row.label: ACCELERATION START
row.help: Modern aim: how far you push the stick before the turn speeds up. Default is the game's own, as Classic's.

row.label: FLICK STICK
row.help: Point the right stick and you turn at once to face that way: right, a quarter turn; down, about face. Turn it round its rim and you turn with it. Aim up and down with the gyro.
row.note: With the default stick layout.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: LEFT STICK
row.help: How far the left stick moves before you move. Raise it for a stick that drifts; lower it to start walking sooner. Default is the game's own, 27%.
row.note: The touch controls' stick too.

row.label: RIGHT STICK
row.help: How far the right stick moves before the view turns. Raise it for a stick that drifts; lower it for finer aim. Default is the game's own, 27%.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: PICTURE POSITION
row.help: Where the picture sits on a screen taller than it, such as a folding phone's inner screen or a tablet. Top puts all the black space below it, where the touch controls are; Bottom puts it all above. Portrait always has it near the top, under the strip of buttons.

row.label: PICTURE SHAPE
row.help: The picture's shape on a screen taller than it. 4:3 is the Xbox's; 16:9 sees more to the sides and leaves more of the screen to the touch controls.

row.label: PORTRAIT FRAME
row.help: The look of the screen around the picture when you play in portrait: plain black, Halo's blue lines and rings, or Xbox green. It is never drawn over the picture.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: STREAMER MODE
row.help: Hides offensive words in names and text from other players, maps and mods, as stars.

row.label: SLURS
row.help: Slurs about race, sexuality, gender and disability.

row.label: SWEARING
row.help: Swearing and sexual words. Strong and Worse leaves the mildest showing.

row.label: INSULTS
row.help: Name-calling and insults that are not slurs.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: SHOW FULL GAMES
row.help: Lists the games that have no room left.

row.label: SHOW EMPTY GAMES
row.help: Lists the games that no one is playing yet.

row.label: SHOW PASSWORD GAMES
row.help: Lists the games that need a password to join.

row.label: PING
row.help: Lists only the games whose ping is under this.
row.note: A game whose ping is not known is listed: a local network game's, a dedicated server's, one still being timed.

row.label: TICK RATE
row.help: Lists only the games of this tick rate.
row.note: GOAT H1 games play at 30, 60 or 120 ticks a second; Legacy games are OpenCE's netcode.

row.label: GAME TYPE
row.search_choices: any slayer team capture the flag oddball king of hill race swat infection gun game co op pro 2v2
row.help: Lists only the games of this type.
row.note: Slayer is free for all; SWAT, Infection and Gun Game are OpenCE's. Pro 2v2 is PRO 2V2's games.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: DISCORD
row.help: The Discord account linked to this game, and how many of the master servers it is linked with.

row.label: UNLINK
row.help: Forgets the linked account on this device. Select it twice: the first asks, the second unlinks.

row.label: MASTER 1
row.help: A master server lists dedicated servers. Select it to link your Discord account with it in your browser.

row.label: MASTER 2
row.help: A master server lists dedicated servers. Select it to link your Discord account with it in your browser.

row.label: MASTER 3
row.help: A master server lists dedicated servers. Select it to link your Discord account with it in your browser.

row.label: MASTER 4
row.help: A master server lists dedicated servers. Select it to link your Discord account with it in your browser.

row.label: SHOW TO SERVERS
row.help: Which servers see your Discord name. When Asked: only a server that blocks VPNs, when you join it from one. Never: such a server refuses you on a VPN.

button.help: Puts this page's settings back to their defaults.
Saves your changes, on this page and every tab, and applies them.
Goes back without these changes.

row.label: HANDS:
row.help: Aiming with the controller, your hands: with arms from the shoulders, floating, or the game's arms.

row.label: AIM:
row.help: What aims: the right controller, which holds the weapon, your head, or a gamepad's right stick.

row.label: GAMEPAD VIEW:
row.help: With a gamepad, the right stick turns and pitches the view, only turns it, or in steps.

row.label: TWO-HANDED AIM:
row.help: The left grip holds a long gun by its foregrip: it aims along the line between your hands.

row.label: AIM ASSIST:
row.help: Near an enemy your aim is slow to leave it, and zoomed, it is drawn gently toward it.

row.label: SWING TO MELEE:
row.help: A hard swing of the right controller melees, as B does; with its grip held, a softer one will do.

row.label: HOLSTERS:
row.help: Reach over your right shoulder for a long gun, or to your right hip for a pistol, and grip to draw it.

row.label: PHYSICAL CROUCH:
row.help: Crouch in the room and you crouch in the game; stand up and you stand.

row.label: SCOPES:
row.help: Smart-link: the right stick's click zooms on your visor. At the eye: raise the scope to your eye.

row.label: RELOAD BY HAND:
row.help: Take a magazine from your left hip and push it in: loaded at once. X still reloads.

row.label: TURNING:
row.help: How the right stick turns you: in steps, or continuously.

row.label: SNAP TURN ANGLE:
row.help: How far each snap turn turns you.

row.label: SMOOTH TURN SPEED:
row.help: How fast smooth turning turns you, the stick pushed all the way: degrees a second.

row.label: VEHICLE VIEW:
row.help: In a vehicle's seat, the view from your head, or the game's camera following the vehicle.

row.label: DEATH VIEW:
row.help: As you die, the view stays where your head was (turned to your body in a blink), or the game's.

row.label: HAND, HEIGHT, HUD...
row.help: The hand that holds the weapon, your height, the world's scale, the HUD, the menus, the resolution.

row.label: DOMINANT HAND:
row.help: The hand that holds the weapon. Left: mirrored, the holsters at your left, the magazines at your right.

row.label: SWAP STICKS:
row.help: Move with the right stick and turn with the left: by default, with the left hand dominant.

row.label: POSITION (RESTART):
row.help: Seated: your eyes where they are when you recentre. From the next time the game starts.

row.label: EYE HEIGHT:
row.help: Standing, the height of your eyes above the floor.

row.label: WORLD SCALE:
row.help: How large the world looks: more than 1 makes it larger, and you smaller in it.

row.label: HUD DISTANCE:
row.help: How far in front of your eyes the HUD is.

row.label: HUD SIZE:
row.help: How wide the HUD is, in degrees of your view.

row.label: MENU DISTANCE:
row.help: How far in front of you the menus are.

row.label: MENU WIDTH:
row.help: How wide the menus are.

row.label: RESOLUTION (RESTART):
row.help: Of the size the headset recommends: less is faster, more sharper. From the next start.

row.label: REFRESH RATE (RESTART):
row.help: The headset's rate, if it offers it; the game draws a frame each refresh. From the next start.

row.label: HUD AND VISOR...
row.help: The HUD on your helmet's visor: its depths, its glass and glow, the helmet's rim, the shields' energy.

row.label: HUD:
row.help: On your helmet's visor, curved about your eyes, or a flat screen before them.

row.label: HUD DEPTH:
row.help: How far apart in depth the HUD's parts are: the tracker nearest, the waypoints farthest.

row.label: HUD WRAP:
row.help: The HUD's corners turned out along the visor's curve, toward the edges of your view.

row.label: HUD LAG:
row.help: How far the HUD trails your head's turns.

row.label: HUD GLOW:
row.help: The HUD's glow on the visor's glass.

row.label: HUD ON GLASS:
row.help: The HUD as light on the glass: the world through it, the glass's tint, its bloom and reflection.

row.label: HUD REACTS:
row.help: More contrast in bright light, dimmer in the dark, a flicker as your shields are hit.

row.label: HELMET RIM:
row.help: The helmet's faceplate about the visor, at the edges of your view, in depth.

row.label: RIM DEPTH:
row.help: How far before your eyes the helmet's rim is.

row.label: VISOR SHADE:
row.help: The helmet's shadow on the glass at the edges of your view, and the glass's faint gold.

row.label: SHIELD EFFECTS:
row.help: The shields on the glass: their energy, the red warning, the HUD's flicker as they break.

row.label: SHIELD ENERGY:
row.help: How strong the shields' energy across the glass is, as they are hit and as they recharge.

row.label: TURNING:
row.help: How the right stick turns you: in steps, or continuously.

row.label: SNAP TURN ANGLE:
row.help: How far each snap turn turns you.

row.label: SMOOTH TURN SPEED:
row.help: How fast smooth turning turns you, the stick pushed all the way: degrees a second.

row.label: COMFORT VIGNETTE:
row.help: The edges of your view dim a little as a vehicle turns you fast, speeds up or slows hard.

row.label: POSITION (RESTART):
row.help: Seated: your eyes where they are when you recentre. From the next time the game starts.

row.label: EYE HEIGHT:
row.help: Standing, the height of your eyes above the floor.
